entries.text: On October 13, 2026, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), and the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced regulatory resolutions related to certain aspects of the Corporation’s U.S. Bank Secrecy Act, Anti-Money Laundering and Economic Sanctions Compliance Programs (Programs). These resolutions included consent orders with the OCC and FinCEN and a settlement agreement with OFAC. As a result, for the third quarter of 2026, the Corporation recorded a $1.2 billion non-tax-deductible charge in noninterest expense to accrue for the civil money penalties resulting from the regulatory consent orders and the settlement agreement (“regulatory settlement charge”).

FinCEN’s consent order and the previously disclosed December 2024 OCC consent order require the Corporation to undertake certain remedial actions to the Programs, including engaging independent consultants to review certain historical transactions, customer due diligence, foreign correspondent account due diligence, and Bank Secrecy Act/anti-money laundering data governance. The Corporation has completed significant steps to satisfy the requirements of the December 2024 OCC consent order. Since late 2023, the Corporation has increased the number of personnel dedicated to these activities and has made investments in technology and other resources supporting the remediation and ongoing compliance. The Corporation does not expect that the ongoing operating costs associated with these remediation and compliance activities will have a significant impact on consolidated noninterest expense in future periods.
